escalations.reason: Current Definition incorrectly calls every standard-chart trace an affine curve with nonconstant defining polynomial: F=x_i has empty trace on D_+(x_i), with dehomogenisation 1. Current scaling Remark also identifies V(x_0^2) with the single point (0:0:1), although it is the line V(x_0). Chart clause must permit empty traces and the concrete projective-zero-set example must be corrected.

Current Statement (d), Facts F3 and step 2.2 pair A(C),A(D) with A^{-1}p. Under the ordinary image convention used by its direct consumer lem-projective-coordinate-invariance-bezout-sum, the corresponding point is A(p). Example translating x=0 and p=(0,0) by x -> x+1 sends curve to x=1 and point to (1,0), not (-1,0). Current coordinate convention must be made consistent.

Current step 3.1 reverses the quotient factorisation: m^s subset (f,g) implies O -> O/m^s -> O/(f,g), not the asserted O -> O/(f,g) -> O/m^s. Containment argument and Statement are sound, but this proof sentence is false.

Current definition declares a DVR valuation on k(C)^× for a possibly reducible reduced plane curve C. A reducible curve has no single function field k(C); the fraction field of O_C,p is the function field of its unique component through smooth p. This valuation domain must be specified without narrowing the allowed curves.

Current Remark falsely claims the tangent line at any smooth point cannot lie in C. For C=V(xy), a point on one component away from crossing is smooth and its tangent is that component. The definition I_p>=3 also admits infinite intersection multiplicity, contrary to its line-no-flex conclusion. Flex and bitangent clauses must require finite contacts/no line component, retaining reducible curves.

Current Statement universally asserts I_p(C,T)=ord_p(F|T) at every smooth point. For C a line or a reducible curve with a line component smooth at p, T is contained in C and F|T=0, so the asserted finite vanishing order is undefined. F3 and proof incorrectly deny this case; statement must retain line/no-flex clause while making finite-contact identity conditional.

Current family calls V(F) a plane curve of degree d for every nonzero F in arbitrary W subset degree-d forms, conflicting with def-plane-projective-curve reduced squarefree convention: W=span(x0^2) gives reduced line of degree one. Need explicit scheme/divisor convention for linear systems or correct reduced-member degree treatment. Remark also incorrectly says P^{r+1} of forms has system dimension r (it has r+1).

Current Remark (a) universally asserts the affine intersection sum is strictly below de. This holds only if intersection points actually lie outside the affine chart; two nonparallel affine lines meeting at a finite point have affine sum de=1. Need state missing-at-infinity condition or weak inequality.

Current step 1.1 invokes symmetry x -> -x of f=y^2-x^2-x^3 to obtain the other tangent-line value. That map does not preserve f. The result is correct via y -> -y or direct substitution y=-x, but the supplied argument is false.

Current F2 falsely says the three coordinate lines are disjoint in projective plane. They meet at coordinate vertices. Their intersections with the Fermat cubic are disjoint because no vertex lies on the cubic; this must be the counting argument.

Current proof step1.1 falsely says a sequence whose tails lie in a fixed I^N A is Cauchy and hence convergent. In A=C[[t]], I=(t), alternating 0,t stays in I A but is not Cauchy modulo t^2. The required convergence criterion is eventually fixed modulo every I^n A; the subsequent explicit binomial series does satisfy it.

Current step3.1 braid table swaps the rows b<c<a and c<a<b. For w=(3,1,2), successive rho_i,rho_j,rho_i give (v-1)^2 E_j+v(v-1)(E+E_ji)+v^2 E_iji; current b<c<a row instead gives (v-1)^2 E_i+v(v-1)(E+E_ij)+v^2 E_iji. The reverse row is similarly swapped. Correct table required for the local finite verification of the defining braid relation.

Current step2.1 gets covariance scaling wrong: f_{gb}=chi(b) f_g from the defining normalized functions, not chi(b)^{-1} f_g. Current step3.2 also asserts w in W_chi normalizes B and U, false for chi=1 and any nontrivial adjacent transposition. Thus e_chi w e_chi=e_chi w and its nonzero coefficient proof fail. The sound Statement needs a valid intertwiner identification and stabilizer-corner basis proof.

Current representative comparison asserts chi(b1^-1 b1prime)=chi(b2 b2prime^-1)^-1, but conjugation compatibility gives equality without the inverse. With that corrected, the asserted equality of products of scalar compensators follows. Current written comparison is false.

Current step1.1 reverses mixed-corner orientation: Hom(Ae_chiprime,Ae_chi) corresponds to e_chiprime A e_chi. Step2.1 coefficient calculation falsely sums over all B and gives 1/|B| instead of intersection-subgroup cardinality/|B|^2; conjugation is defined only on the intersection and chi=w chi_prime does not imply w chi=chi_prime. Endomorphism and Hom basis Statements are sound but these arguments need replacement.

Current F3 claims for n=2 and any torus character W_chi=S2, false for unequal coordinates (e.g. q=3 with chi=(1,nontrivial)). The equal-coordinate Given suffices and should qualify the fact. Current proof step2.2 also says left B invariance alone implies f(b1 s b2)=f(s), omitting right covariance scalar.

Current step3.1 writes B_u B_v=R_Theta(v^-1) R_Theta(u^-1), reversing the operators themselves although definition is B_u=R_Theta(u^-1). Correct reversed corner product is obtained from R_Theta(u^-1) R_Theta(v^-1)=R_(Theta(v^-1)Theta(u^-1)). Statement and preceding corner product are sound.

Current step1.3 uses undefined D,C in tensor products and says B=C[z,1/(fd)] maps to A without localizing A at d. Current step2.1 applies Nullstellensatz to J=I(Zx) and then evaluates an identity in defining generators without proving membership in their ideal. Need use defining equation ideal and strong Nullstellensatz radical membership, plus explicit bilinear multiplicativity equations and R,C tensor factors.

Current F5 assigns spherical unit R_eB eigenvalues q and -1, although R_eB is identity and has only eigenvalue 1. It must be R_Ts. Current step2.1 also falsely says e_UP acts as identity by left multiplication on C[G]e_eta; only its action in the relevant corner/right multiplication is needed.

Current step1.2 denies a basis-preserving isomorphism without its Statement restriction n>=2: for n=1 both algebras equal C and the unit basis does match. Current step2.1 falsely says composing with any automorphism changes simple-module bijection; inner automorphisms preserve simple isomorphism classes.

Current step2.1 falsely says unit T1 lies in linear span of Ts, despite these being the two independent basis elements established in step1.1. The unital algebra generated by Ts contains unit by definition, which proves intended generation.

Current step5.1 concludes integral c_U(chi1-chi2) is nonzero from positive cutoff and a lower bound on absolute value alone. Complex cancellation invalidates that inference; need rotated positive-real-part control in a sufficiently small neighbourhood or use the already-proved translation-ratio reconstruction to establish injectivity.

Current uniqueness step6.1 integrates h=h0+c against the extended PVM as integral h0 + c P({infinity})=T(h0). The constant function integrates to c P(Xplus)=cI, so equality with Tplus(h) needs that term. Existing formula is false even for h=1.
Current step5.1 asserts phi^-1(V) phi^-1(V)^-1=phi^-1(VV^-1), false for a nonsurjective homomorphism. The required containment is valid and sufficient; correct equality to inclusion.

Current F1 indexes fundamental family by j<k(x) while constant k=r is said to have complete family e1,...,er. With one-based coordinates j<=k(x) is required; current definition loses one dimension for every finite k, including k=1. Also mixed-space decomposition requires apply commutant theorem to block operator on sum field rather than treating U_B as endomorphism of one field.

Current step4.1 sends L2(nu0)->L2(nu) by multiplication sqrt(dnu/dnu0), which is the wrong density for an isometry in that direction. It needs sqrt(dnu0/dnu). Current steps1.3 and3.2 also use multiplicity m and Uprime before their constructions; fields must be restricted/extended across null complements with Borel values.

Current step1.1 claims a separating family itself defines every orbit as intersection of members containing it, while silently replacing separating sets by complements not in family. Need explicitly adjoin complements to form the countable defining family, which preserves intended equivalence.

Current step3.2 obtains a globally positive continuous probability density on arbitrary noncompact H from compactly supported cutoffs. A single compactly supported cutoff cannot be positive Haar-a.e. on noncompact H; need countable weighted cutoff construction or an arbitrary strictly positive integrable Borel density. Current matrix unitary equations also omit cross terms.

Current step2.1 incorrectly replaces supremum over image of Delta(A) in Nhat by supremum over all Nhat. Arbitrary pi is not faithful: the trivial representation has ||pi(f)||=|integral f|, not ||fhat||infinity. Only <= is valid and sufficient for extension. Current step1.2 uses P before construction; step5.1 needs phase rotation to ensure a nonzero real integral for imaginary-valued h.

Current step1.1 maps the dense continuous covariant model by Borel indicators and concludes it extends to its completion, without establishing the resulting generally discontinuous covariant sections belong to that completion. Need identify completion with measurable L2 sections using density supplier or supply approximation argument; bounded norm alone does not establish codomain membership.

Current proof step1.2 asserts constant-multiplicity existence before steps2-5 establish it, so numbered proof has a forward dependency and uses unconstructed K. Move this conclusion/uniqueness after constant multiplicity has been proved; later argument gives intended sound result.

Current step1.1 claims continuity of g->sqrt(d(Lg)_*mu/dmu) in L-infinity class for arbitrary equivalent finite mu. Densities may be unbounded and not L-infinity continuous; strong continuity of Vg follows from unitary transport from the rho measure and is sufficient. The field construction should use that valid premise.

Current step3.1 computes h(s(x),eH)=s(x) and evaluates sigma(s(x)), generally outside its domain H. The definition gives h(s(x),eH)=s(x)^-1 s(x)=e, yielding Bx as required. Current trivial-H boundary also calls it unique equivalence of one-dimensional scalars, despite arbitrary fibre K.

Current F4 and step1.1 call the field B a field of scalars and say both B and f are scalar multiplications. Bx is an arbitrary unitary operator on K; it commutes with scalar multiplier f because f(x)I commutes with Bx, not because Bx is scalar.

Current proof step1.4 labels sigma(s(x)^-1 g s(g^-1 x)) as the source-variable cocycle. This is the target-variable multiplier; source cocycle is sigma(s(gx)^-1 g s(x)). At eH for h in H they agree, but the claimed canonical cocycle formula must match the supplier convention.

Current F3 repeats the target-variable formula sigma(s(x)^-1 g s(g^-1 x)) as the source-variable cocycle used by Haar regularization. The source convention is sigma(s(gx)^-1 g s(x)); mixed conventions must be corrected before the gauge uniqueness argument is applied.

Current verification step1.2 calls coordinate multipliers M_xj bounded operators on L2(Rn), false for n>=1; they are unbounded self-adjoint with domains {f:xj f in L2} and need unbounded spectral-integral treatment. Step1.1 writes indicator E(x+t) while identifying it with P(t+E); correct indicator is E(x-t). Momentum sign/domain convention must be checked against generator supplier.
